correctness.rationale: The explicit graph, 5,887 matchings, augmented boundary ranks and 120 automorphism signed Lefschetz values are independently reconstructed in the included checkers. Modular lower bounds are proved exact over Q by adjacent-rank saturation; rational character decomposition has exact integer checks including Schur index/Galois normalization. An independently entered 30-edge graph list and exact mod-three antipodal eigenspace calculation establish the unique odd H4(F3) class. The natural UCT identifies it with the 3-torsion in H3(Z) using the explicitly cited prior integral theorem; A5 perfectness forces trivial torsion action.

evidence: Shareshian–Wachs, arxiv:math/0409054, studies complete-graph matching complexes and chessboard complexes with representation-theoretic methods; neither has the icosahedral matching complex as a direct instance.

Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega, arxiv:2411.04601, proves outerplanar graph matching complexes have sphere-wedge homotopy type. The icosahedron has 30 edges, while a 12-vertex outerplanar graph has at most 21.

The new graph automorphism character and central torsion sign do not follow from that result. value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is a canonical symmetric planar graph with exceptional order-three torsion in its matching complex. Resolving the full rational automorphism character and central inversion on its characteristic torsion subgroup is meaningful structural equivariant topology, not a numerical tweak; the odd torsion action is invisible in rational homology and the rational representation is not determined by the known wedge/Moore type.
